memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then the officers who were over the units of the army—the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds—went to Moses and said to him, "Your servants have counted the soldiers under our command, and not one is missing. So we have brought as an offering to the Lord the gold articles each of us acquired—armlets, bracelets, signet rings, earrings and necklaces—to make atonement for ourselves before the Lord." - Num 31:48-50 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The commanders came to Moses with an astonishing report: they had counted every soldier, and not one was missing. In a battle of that scale, this was nothing short of miraculous. Overwhelmed with gratitude, they responded not by keeping their gold but by bringing it as an offering to the Lord. Thankfulness naturally overflowed into giving.

There is a lovely instinct here that we would do well to imitate. When God protects and provides, the fitting response is worship and generosity, not pride or forgetfulness. It is so easy to receive a mercy and quickly move on, forgetting to thank the One who gave it. These officers stopped, recognised God's hand, and returned something to Him as an act of grateful worship.

Notice their words — they brought their gold "to make atonement for ourselves before the Lord." They knew that even in victory they were sinners in need of God's mercy. Their gold could not truly atone, of course; it was a humble acknowledgement of their need. That need is fully met in Jesus, who made atonement once for all by His own blood (Heb 9:12). We can offer nothing to purchase our forgiveness; He has already purchased it completely.

So we give today not to buy God's favour, but as grateful worship to the One who has already saved us. Every offering flows from a heart that says thank you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When God protects or provides for you, is your first instinct gratitude?
2. Do you ever try to "earn" what Christ has already freely given?
3. What offering of thanks can you bring to God today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Gracious God, thank You for Your protection and provision, and above all for the atonement Jesus made for me. Fill my heart with gratitude that overflows into worship and generosity. Amen.
